items.title: Rams TE Tyler Higbee is considered week-to-week with a chest injury he suffered in Week 12’s win over the Packers.
items.text: ESPN’s Adam Schefter was the first to report the news on Higbee. Higbee will reportedly have “a chance” to play in Week 13 against the Chiefs, but as Schefter reported, that decision will be based on “how he heals over the next week.” Where things stand right now, the Rams are currently down three tight ends, with Terrance Ferguson (ankle) out for the season and Davis Allen (ankle) also considered week-to-week after going down in Week 12. items.title: Rams TE Davis Allen is considered week-to-week after suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 12’s win over the Packers.
items.text: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport was the first to report the news. Allen will reportedly go to the Rams’ facilities today for a full evaluation to determine the approximate length of his absence, but with Terrance Ferguson (ankle) out for the season and Tyler Higbee (chest) also considered week-to-week, the Rams are suddenly very thin at tight end. Rookie second-rounder Max Klare and veteran Colby Parkinson are the only healthy tight ends currently on the roster, but it’s possible the Rams will look to add one or two more free agents to fill their needs at the position. items.title: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle/groin) will not play in Week 12 against the Dolphins.
items.text: With a Week 13 bye on tap for the Jets, the team is hoping two extra weeks of rest will be more than enough for Cooper to play in Week 14 against the Broncos. Cooper has not played since re-injuring his ankle in Week 10 against the Bills and has now missed six of a possible 12 games in his rookie season. It’s possible this is the last update we receive on Cooper until the Jets return from their bye week, but fantasy managers in need of help over the next two weeks can safely drop him where needed. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said he’s “not sure yet” if Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) will play in Week 12 against the Titans.
items.text: Fantasy managers don’t need to panic just yet. The Jaguars have not taken the field for their Friday practice, and Coen said the team will assess how he looks on Friday before making any further decisions on his availability. Tuten has not practiced in either of the first two practices of the week, so a limited practice would be a slight upgrade for him heading into the weekend. We will check back in with a final update on his availability when the team announces it, but backup Chris Rodriguez could be in line for a busy week if Tuten were to be sidelined. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: Parker Washington (shoulder) will not play in the Jaguars’ Week 12 game against the Titans.
items.text: According to head coach Liam Coen, Washington aggravated an AC joint injury in Thursday’s practice that will sideline him for at least one week. Speaking with the media on Friday, Coen said the team hopes to have him back “ASAP” but noted that it is a “week-to-week injury.” Jakobi Meyers could be first in line to benefit from Washington’s absence, but this certainly isn’t an ideal situation for fantasy managers with the fantasy playoffs just weeks away. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: Dallas Goedert (shoulder) was spotted in a sling after the Eagles’ Week 12 win over the Cowboys.
items.text: Goedert exited Week 12’s win over the Cowboys with a shoulder injury on the first drive of the game. The veteran tight end did not return to the game, and the fact that he was wearing a sling after the game suggests this could be somewhat of a serious injury. Head coach Nick Sirianni did not comment on his injury after the game, so it’s possible we won’t learn until later next week what he’s dealing with and how much time he could miss, if any. items.title: Rashee Rice caught 2-of-5 targets for 19 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills.
items.text: Rice’s quiet day was made all the worse by the refs when they overturned his third catch to an incomplete pass after replay showed the ball hitting the ground. While the tip of the ball did touch the turf, the ball didn’t appear to move. While the controversial call eventually led to a Buffalo victory, calling it a catch would have changed little for fantasy managers. Rice has played five games since returning from his early-season hamstring injury. He had more than 53 yards in just one of them. items.title: Travis Kelce caught 4-of-7 targets for 71 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills.
items.text: Kelce was the only member of the Chiefs’ passing attack to find any success in this game. Being battered by the elements, Patrick Mahomes relied on his trusted tight end for a handful of big plays throughout the contest. One of them was a 21-yard toss to the nine-yard line at the end of the first half that set up a short field goal. Kelce, however, paid the price with a helmet to the back that left him on the ground in pain for a while. items.title: Ty Johnson caught both of his targets for 12 yards in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
items.text: Johnson spiked for 55 yards on seven catches last week. That usage was nowhere to be found on Thanksgiving. It was a rain-soaked rock-fight of a game in which the Bills barely even tried to pass. Josh Allen threw the ball 21 times and only 10 were caught. The low volume axed any chance Johnson had of an encore. Facing a lowly Patriots team in Week 13, we don’t expect much work for Buffalo’s third-down back next week. Johnson will be buried in the RB5 ranks. - Kyle Dvorchak

items.title: Khalil Shakir caught 3-of-6 targets for 33 yards in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
items.text: Shakir led the Bills in targets, catches, and yards, but it was a memorable Thanksgiving for the worst kind of reason. Josh Allen tossed him a simple screen pass in the red zone late in the third quarter, but Shakir failed to corral the ball and bobbled it right into the hands of Chiefs corner Nohl Williams. The good news for Shakir is that the blunder didn’t land him in the doghouse. Allen’s very next attempt went to Shakir for a six-yard gain.
